title: Shut spring kitchen tongs and draw out the pull tab that locks them
instruction: Lock the kitchen tongs shut. Squeeze the two steel arms together, pull the black tab at the hinge end straight out until it stops, then take both grippers away. The lock must then hold the tongs shut on the worktop.
context: Spring tongs are in most kitchens; a pair with a pull-tab lock is locked shut to go in a drawer, as left alone it springs open, here to 84 mm between the tips. Patent US 11,974,682 calls the hinge pull tab the most popular tongs lock and says it takes both hands. The tab reaches its stop only while the arms are within 3 degrees of shut, which takes 4.4 N at 9 cm from the pin; the tab is 13 cm from that hold and moves 12 mm. The tool is loose and weighs 135 g: pulled without a hold, the tab only drags it over the worktop, and arms let go before the tab is out are open again in 0.1 s. The demonstrated way: one hand holds the arms shut while the other draws the tab. Nearest board tasks: TK-ZUZVPW, locking pliers squeezed past an over-centre latch by one gripper (here the other hand draws a separate keeper); TK-M6GCBU, a sprung M.2 drive held down while a latch is turned over it. Here nothing is fixed and the open arms block the keeper.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers (fingers open to 94 mm), bases 61 cm apart, at the station worktop (laminate, 110 x 130 cm). Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the bases: x forward, y left; heights are above the worktop. TONGS: spring tongs with a hinge pull-tab lock, sized after the OXO Good Grips 9-inch tongs (no. 28481): stainless steel with black non-slip grips, 230 mm long with the tab in, 135 g (catalogue figures). Each arm is 1 mm stainless sheet, 32 mm wide before folding, folded to a channel 20 mm wide and 6 mm deep, 200 mm long, with a head 30 mm wide. With its grip, the arm that carries the pin and spring weighs 61 g and the other arm 54 g; the tab with its plate weighs about 20 g. A pin joins the arms 24 mm from their back ends, 176 mm from the tips. A spring at the pin holds them 27.5 degrees open (84 mm between the inner faces of the tips, 111 mm across over the heads) and resists closing with 0.20 N m when open, rising to 0.40 N m shut: 2.3 N at the tips (a spring balance there reads about 230 g), 4.4 N at 9 cm from the pin. LOCK: a black nylon pull tab at the hinge end (a ring 24 x 25 x 8 mm with a 12 x 13 mm hanging hole, on a stem) moves a steel lock plate inside the hinge. Here the lock is pull-to-lock, as in patent US 7,448,660 (Helen of Troy, OXO's owner): a sliding plate drawn rearward holds the arms closed, pushed forward it frees them. With the arms shut the tab pulls 12 mm straight out against about 1 N of friction and then stops them reopening: let go, they spring back 3 degrees (tips 9 mm apart) and hold. Pushing the tab in with the arms squeezed unlocks them. The gap between the hinge end of the arms and the ring is 5 mm with the tab in and 17 mm with it out. Locked, the tongs measure 242 x 37 x 30 mm. Real bench: a pair of tongs of this size whose tab locks when pulled out, unmodified. In simulation the lock plate is a steel block 18 x 10 x 10.6 mm on the tab that slides under two lugs on the other arm's heel, 20 mm behind the pin and 1 mm clear of them; let go, the lugs rest on it with about 19 N. With the arms 4 degrees or more open the lugs stop the tab 3.8 to 6.3 mm out; it cannot pass 11 mm unless the arms are within 3 degrees of shut. A tab left 6 to 11 mm out can hold the simulated arms on the block's edge, short of its stop; that is not scored as locked. START: the tongs lie open on their side (hinge pin upright), resting on the edges of both heads and of the hinge, tips toward the robot: pin at x 19.0, y +0.5; the inner faces of the two tips at x 2.0, y -4.2 and x 1.8, y +4.2; the arm that the tab's stem lies along is the one at y -4.2; tab in, its ring standing on edge 3 mm clear of the worktop, centred at x 23.3, y +0.4. The arms span heights 0.5 to 2.5 cm, heads and hinge 0 to 3.0 cm. Nothing else is on the worktop, and nothing is fixed to it. The layout is the same in every trial; nothing is hidden. The robot arms start in their ready pose.
scoring: The squeeze is read during the trial, everything else from the final state. A real trial uses the video, a ruler and a side photo. TIP GAP: the gap between the inner faces of the two tips (ruler; 84 mm open, 9 mm resting on the lock). TAB GAP: the gap between the hinge end of the arms and the ring (ruler; 5 mm with the tab in, 17 mm at its stop). SQUEEZED SHUT: at some point of the trial the tip gap stayed at most 14 mm for 1 s (video). Once reached, this is kept. LOCK ENGAGED, at the end: the tab is within 1 mm of its stop, the ruler's reading allowance (tab gap at least 16 mm), and the tip gap is at most 14 mm. A tab short of that is not locked, whatever the arms do. The tab cannot be out that far unless the arms are within 3 degrees of shut, so a gripper that only holds the arms shut cannot produce this reading. LET GO: throughout the last 1 s, every point of both grippers' fingers is at least 3 cm from every part of the tongs (video); a gripper that cannot be read counts as not let go. STILL: over the last 1 s the tongs moved less than 2 mm and turned less than 2 degrees (video), and the tip gap and the tab gap read the same to 1 mm on two photos taken 1 s apart. ON THE WORKTOP: the tongs lie on the worktop, their lowest point within 1 mm of its surface (side photo). NOT FALLEN: no part of the tongs is more than 1 cm below the level of the worktop. 1.0: lock engaged, let go, still and on the worktop. The trial ends as a success once this has held for 1 s. 0.5: lock engaged and not fallen, but not all of the rest: a gripper is still within 3 cm of the tongs, or they are still moving, or they are held up or lie on a gripper. The lock is in place but has not been left to hold by itself. 0.25: not fallen and squeezed shut at some point, but the lock is not engaged at the end. 0: anything else. That includes doing nothing; a tab pulled with the arms open; and tongs, locked or not, that ended on the floor. Nothing zeroes the whole trial: no step here can hurt a person or the tool, so a robot that fumbles or lets the tongs spring open may try again. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. the hinge spring is a joint spring (0.42 N m/rad, 0.20 N m open to 0.40 N m shut, damping 0.03 N m s/rad); the tab is a slider with 1 N friction; the lock plate is a block under two heel lugs, held by contact. Arms are 20 x 6 mm bars, heads 30 x 30 x 14 mm blocks; one friction, 0.6; no arm flex. Pull-to-lock is ours; OXO sets only the size. Length and mass are catalogue figures; other sizes, masses, forces and the lock travel are our estimates.
reset_notes: Nothing is used up. Squeeze the arms shut, push the black tab in until it stops and let the arms spring open. Lay the tongs on their side (hinge pin upright) with the pin at x 19.0, y +0.5 cm and the tips toward the robot, their inner faces at y -4.2 and y +4.2. The arm that the tab's stem lies along is the one at y -4.2; the ring's centre is then at x 23.3, y +0.4.
